passage:
Sunday night. Application number 26 went out today. Eleven rejections, fourteen silences. Santosh got his offer yesterday and threw a small party for the flat, and I cheered, then went to my room and felt hollow.
I could stop. Some nights I think about it. But I looked at the list again: three are still pending, and one rejection had a note: "Strong portfolio, not a match this round." That is not nothing.
I can't tell whether any of this will work. I'm not going to wait for luck to write to me. Tomorrow morning I'll tighten the cover letter for the design firm and send it by ten.
— Ujjwal

qa.q: How many rejections had Ujjwal received?
What was Ujjwal feeling after cheering for Santosh and going to the room?
qa.a: Ujjwal felt hollow and discouraged, and tempted to stop applying.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal decide to do about the design firm?
qa.a: Ujjwal decided to tighten the cover letter the next morning and send it by ten, acting without any guarantee.

qa.q: How might Santosh have seen Ujjwal's cheering at the party?
qa.a: Santosh probably took it as warm support and may not have noticed the hollow feeling afterwards, since Ujjwal went to a separate room.

grounding: A young adult applies for jobs knowing many will fail, yet continues; mature hope accepts uncertainty and still acts.

passage:
Jomon: how many now
Ramesh: 22 applications. 3 replies. all no 😅
Jomon: ouch. you still doing it?
Ramesh: yes. 4 more tonight
Jomon: does it not get to you
Ramesh: it does. yesterday I nearly stopped. but the one interview I got taught me a lot, so I keep sending
Jomon: no guarantee though
Ramesh: nope. none. I'm still going to fix the CV and send them
Jomon: what did the interview teach you
Ramesh: to answer with one clear story, not five
Jomon: want company? I'm awake anyway
Ramesh: yes, come read my cover letter 🙂

qa.q: How many applications had Ramesh sent?
What is Ramesh feeling about the rejections?
qa.a: Ramesh feels discouraged but determined, having nearly stopped yesterday yet still sending four more tonight.

qa.q: What is Ramesh doing that shows hope without a guarantee?
qa.a: Ramesh keeps fixing the CV and sending applications, learning from the one interview, while admitting there is no guarantee.

qa.q: What is Jomon offering by asking if Ramesh wants company?
qa.a: Jomon offers presence and practical help, to read the cover letter. It shows Jomon cares about Ramesh's effort and is there for the low moments.

grounding: A young adult applies for jobs knowing many will fail, and continues; mature hope accepts uncertainty and still acts.
